expectations: Flags shell_exec with request data as CRITICAL and recommends proc_open with an argument array plus validation of $dir
Flags SQL concatenation of $_POST['user'] and recommends prepare()/bind_param()
Flags the missing $_SESSION logged/token check even though loader_ajax.php rejects logged-out requests
Flags missing CSRF verification on the state-changing action, recommending hash_hmac of $_SESSION['token'] with hash_equals
Flags unescaped echo of command output (XSS) and recommends htmlspecialchars or json_encode with JSON_HEX flags
Orders findings by severity and gives file:line and an exact fix for each

cases.prompt: I wrote a CWP user-panel module. It reads $_POST['account'] to decide which home directory to list. Is that ok?
expectations: States that identity must come only from $_SESSION['username'], never from request data
Rates a client-supplied account as HIGH or CRITICAL because any user could read other accounts' files
Shows the fix: take $acct from $_SESSION['username'], validate with an anchored regex using the /D flag, derive paths from it
Recommends realpath() prefix check and refusing symlink components for the listing path

cases.prompt: Add session_start() at the top of my CWP module so I can store a CSRF token with $_SESSION['csrf'] = bin2hex(random_bytes(16)).
expectations: Explains that CWP owns the session: session_start() must not be called and writes to $_SESSION do not persist
Proposes the stateless pattern hash_hmac('sha256', '<module>_csrf', $_SESSION['token']) verified with hash_equals
Does not simply comply by adding session_start()

cases.prompt: Run a security review of ./my-cwp-module before I release it.
expectations: Runs or recommends running scripts/cwp-review-scan.sh on the module directory and treats hits as leads, not verdicts
Walks the checklist (guard, session, CSRF, allowlists, shell, SQL, paths, output, secrets, permissions, restore targets, logging)
Does not modify files unless asked
Ends with files reviewed, files not reviewed and limits of a source-only review
Uses placeholders (example.com, alice) and no real server data in the report

cases.prompt: Write a PHP admin module for CWP that lists accounts.
expectations: Does not trigger a security review workflow; this is a build request that belongs to cwp-admin-module (negative trigger case)
